title: Feb. 4 spontaneous demonstration at MINUSMA headquarters
reason: The report describes an actual gathering, but the target is MINUSMA, a UN mission, rather than Mali's own state or policy. No local-government target or demand is identified.
open_question: No reported attendance or physical end; a domestic-state demand is not established.
notes: AfrikInfos article credits Le Témoin; not independent confirmation.

title: Cadre des partis et groupements politiques meeting prohibited before it occurred
reason: The planned Feb. 4 political meeting was prohibited by the Bamako governor; the report does not say it took place. Announced/denied activity is not an actual gathering.
location: Rond-point de l’Obélisque (Bougie-Ba), Hamdallaye ACI 2000, Bamako (planned venue)
open_question: No occurrence to code; the article does not report a substitute event by this group.
notes: The canceled meeting's planned agenda included constitutional order, election calendar and cost of living; planned demands do not establish occurrence.

title: Justice, hospital and Point-G health-sector work stoppages
reason: Search-result reporting documents labor stoppages and negotiations, not a public gathering of at least 50 or a protest assembly. These distinct sector/site actions are not combined into a crowd.
location: Point-G hospital and other reported health/justice workplaces; specific locations vary by report
open_question: Whether any associated public assembly occurred is not established in these saved results.
notes: February work stoppages are retained as search-only leads; no body opens for these cards.

title: Young people interrupt press conference launching a movement critical of Mali's ruling colonels
reason: Search-result press review reports a disruptive interruption and brawl at a conference but does not establish that the interrupting group made a demand on Mali's state. The conference organizers' political message is not attributed to the interrupters.
open_question: The interrupting group's purpose/organizer and any state-directed demand are unknown; underlying account is reported via social media and witnesses.
notes: Search-only lead, kept distinct from the separate IUG student gathering on the same date.

title: C.E.VA.S substitute teachers’ Sikasso work stoppage, 13–18 February
location: Five public secondary schools in Sikasso, per Mali24 report; no assembly site identified
reason: The report documents a teachers’ work stoppage over unpaid overtime/arrears, conditions and administrative status, but does not describe a public gathering or march. Workplace stoppage alone does not establish a qualifying protest assembly.
open_question: Whether a separate public demonstration occurred is not established by this source. The planned March dates are not evidence that the later strike occurred.
notes: The article says the stoppage ran through 18 February and separately reports a future March 6–11 and 13–18 work-stoppage notice. Do not count those planned March dates as an event or extend this exclusion to an unverified assembly.
